newsitem.title: FRANCE: Monod wants Suez/Lyonnaise merger agreed Friday.
newsitem.headline: Monod wants Suez/Lyonnaise merger agreed Friday.

text.p: The chairman of French utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux said on Tuesday he hoped a merger with conglomerate Suez would be agreed on Friday, to create a global player with Suez boss Gerard Mestrallet as chief executive.
Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod dispelled media speculation that the merged company -- already agreed in principle -- would be run by a single executive board headed by himself.
Monod made the comments in an interview published in Le Figaro newspaper, in which he also said he wanted the new company to be called Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux.
"We have to rise up to the challenge of a new strategy with global ambitions, of running a new company, Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux, as that will be its offical name...," Monod said.

The merger would bring together Lyonnaise, a sprawling empire embracing electricity, water supply and construction, and Suez, a holding company which is seeking a raison d'etre after selling off key assets such as investment bank Banque Indosuez.
The boards have a meeting scheduled for Friday where they are expected to finalise the terms of a merger.
Monod told Le Figaro he hoped the two firms would quickly meet the challenge of a global market where the large players were operational groups rather than holding companies.
"The big global groups are operations-based ones, focused on a few areas, rather than companies of industrial holdings," he told the newspaper. "France is behind the times on this."

"The new group will have 200 billion francs ($34.6 billion) in sales after the merger, employing 190,000," he said. This had required serious reflection on how to manage the group into the 21st century.
"I have therefore chosen the formula of a supervisory and executive board," he said. The executive board would deal with operational issues and the supervisory board with strategy.

"I am convinced this is the most appropriate formula for the long-term success of this merger," he said. "This decision will take immediate effect from June 1997, before the normal expiry date of my mandate at Lyonnaise, which is September 1998."

Monod did not make it clear what precisely his own position would be. "Regarding myself, it's not a departure, it's a change. I will take take charge, for as long as is necessary, of seeing Suez-Lyonnaise enter the 21st century.

"I want the merger to be decided on Friday," he said, adding that he would work with Gerard Mestrallet "as future head of the executive board" on getting the merger prepared for the annual shareholder meetings in June.

Monod said nothing of the terms on which the merger was likely to be carried out. Newspapers believe the transaction could be carried on the basis of a share parity of 41 Suez shares for 20 Lyonnaise, accompanied by a special payout from Suez to sweeten the deal for Suez shareholders.
Some of those same media reports, however, said the merged group was expected to have a single board headed by Monod. ($ = 5.772 French Francs)
